title: Always With Me: chords and your first flat

blocks.text:
Back to the waltz, now reading its chords: six of them, and a black key in the key signature.

**By the end** you can name and play its six chords and play bars 1–10 with both hands.
# Warm up: the first eight bars

# A flat
The **♭** at the start of each staff, on the B line or space, is the key signature: every B is played as **B flat**, the black key just left of B. The left hand's B♭ chord uses it.

# The chords
Bars 1–10 go **F, F, F, C, Dm, Am, B♭, F, Gm, C**. The arrangement plays each chord above the bass note, not always from its letter up; learn them as it voices them:

- **F**: F A C
- **C**: G C E
- **Dm**: A D F
- **Am**: A C E
- **B♭**: F B♭ D
- **Gm**: G B♭ D

blocks.title: The six chords, by name

blocks.title: Bars 1–10 in time

blocks.text:
# If this happens
- **You play B, not B flat.** The key signature means every B.
- **The chord after the bass note is wrong.** Say the chord's name on beat 1 before you play it.

**Until the next lesson:** the ten bars once a day.
